name: Atumelnant

lead: Atumelnant is an experimental once-daily pill that reduces the adrenal gland's response to ACTH. It is in clinical development for congenital adrenal hyperplasia and Cushing syndrome.
In adults with classic CAH, early studies showed quick, large drops in androstenedione, 17-hydroxyprogesterone and 11-oxygenated androgens, hormones tied to androgen excess.

paras: It antagonizes the ACTH receptor pathway on the adrenal cortex, cutting steroid output. Reviews describe it as a glucocorticoid-sparing approach that could allow lower hydrocortisone replacement doses [2].

As an investigational drug, its safety profile is still being established in phase 2 and 3 studies. Blocking adrenal output requires hormone replacement in the conditions it is being studied for. It is available only through trials.

chain: Blocks ACTH signalling at the adrenal gland
Lowers adrenal androgens such as androstenedione
Less androgen-driven acne and hair growth in CAH
angle.text: For people with CAH, lowering adrenal androgens is the route to clearer skin and more typical hair patterns. This is a trial-stage medicine, and its appearance outcomes have not been reported as endpoints in the sources available.

lead: Atumelnant (CRN04894) is an investigational once-daily oral drug from Crinetics that blocks ACTH signalling in the adrenal glands, which lowers the production of adrenal hormones including androgens [1][2]. It is being developed for congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) and ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome [3][4].

Its relevance to looks is through androgen control. In classic CAH, excess adrenal androgens such as androstenedione and 11-oxygenated androgens are common, and androgen excess is associated with acne and unwanted hair growth. In phase 2 studies atumelnant produced fast reductions in these androgens [5][6].
It is not approved anywhere and is not sold; information comes from company-sponsored trials and endocrinology reviews.

paras: There is no cosmetic use. The appearance-related link is that androgen excess in CAH contributes to acne and hirsutism, and atumelnant lowers the underlying androgens [6].
Studies target classic CAH due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency and ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome [2][4].

Open-label phase 2 results in adults with classic CAH reported rapid, substantial and sustained reductions of androstenedione and 17-hydroxyprogesterone [5][7], reductions of 11-oxygenated androgens [6], and reductions in adrenal volume [8]. In a 10-day inpatient study in ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome, serum and urine cortisol fell [9].

Reviews group atumelnant with CRF1 and ACTH inhibitors, newer glucocorticoid-sparing options alongside crinecerfont, and suggest a block-and-replace strategy with physiologic hydrocortisone dosing [2][10].

Registered studies include a phase 1/2 Cushing study (n=19) [4], the 38-person phase 2 TouCAHn study [11], a phase 2 extension [12], a phase 3 adult study (n=150, started December 2025) [3], a pediatric phase 2/3 study [13], and phase 1 pharmacokinetic and drug-interaction studies [14][15]. Published results are from open-label phase 2 data presented as conference abstracts.

timeline.event: Phase 2 TouCAHn study in CAH and phase 1b/2a Cushing study begin [11][4].
Phase 2 extension starts; interim results report androgen reductions [12][5].
Phase 3 study in adults with CAH begins (December) [3].
